newsitem.title: USA: Congress Republicans OK D.C. tax breaks - paper.
newsitem.headline: Congress Republicans OK D.C. tax breaks - paper.

text.p: Key U.S. Congressional Republicans have decided to approve $325 million in tax breaks for District of Columbia to stimulate its economy, according to senior aides quoted in the Washington Post on Monday.

The Post reported that the proposal will be announced at a news conference later Monday by House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer, R-Texas. The plan would grant federal tax breaks to thousands of individuals and businesses in economically depressed areas of the city, the Post reported.

The proposed tax plan, designed to retain residents and spur job creation and investment in the city, is part of a broader $85 billion federal tax cut plan that is scheduled to be voted on by Archer's panel this week, the Post reported.
The plan includes a targeted income tax cut and a zero percent capital gains tax rate on the sale of certain assets. --U.S. Municipal Desk, 212-859-1650
